hook_text: This bottle of river water looks clear. So why won't the scientist let anyone drink it?
clip_script: Clean-up day on the Hennops River. Bags of plastic, bottles, polystyrene: insoluble pollution you can see. But the scientist tests a clear bottle of water. Dissolved fertiliser! That feeds the algae that choke the dam. And germs from sewage, too small to see, that cause cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea. Clear doesn't mean clean. Toilets, treatment and handwashing keep us safe.
visual_style: Whiteboard river with litter floating on top, then a magnifying circle over clear water revealing dissolved dots and tiny germs.
mood: Determined and caring, like a community clean-up.
pacing: Visible litter first, then the hidden pollution, then the germs.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never pour oil or chemicals down the drain.
